  "overall_assessment": "anomalies",
  "findings": [
    {
      "benefit": "TPD",
      "years": [2022, 2023],
      "pattern": "shock",
      "direction": "increase",
      "magnitude": "flat-topped level jump of ~+0.20 A/E (from ~0.94 baseline to ~1.17) across 2022-2023 (~+20% overpayment), then full reversion to 0.94 in 2024",
      "confidence": 0.9,
      "evidence": [
        "ae_tpd_by_year.csv: 2022 AE=1.173 (1142/974) and 2023 AE=1.161 (1221/1052) vs a 2015-2020 baseline of 0.885-0.969",
        "Evidence pack [TPD]: excursion 2022-2023 +0.218 vs rest of series, score 12.9; both years z+5.4 and z+5.2",
        "ae_tpd_by_year.csv: abrupt 2021->2022 step (+0.144) with no multi-year ramp, flat 2022->2023 (-0.012), sharp 2023->2024 drop (-0.219); 2021 was only a mild uptick (1.029, z+0.9)",
        "summary.json: TPD overall_ae 1.006 masks the 2y bump because offsetting underpayments (2015-2020 ~0.94) balance it out",
        "Co-occurs in the same 2022-2023 window with the IP overpayment (see IP finding), pointing to a shared cause on the two disability lines"
      ],
      "recommended_action": "Run a root-cause review of 2022-2023 TPD experience: decompose A/E into incidence, severity (payment amounts) and duration, and break the 2022-2023 claims down by age/gender and diagnosis (not just the pooled age/gender file) to localize the driver. Check the 2022 policy/claims timeline for a coding, claims-handling or IT change, and for a high-severity/late-reporting cohort. Because 2024 reverts below baseline, decide whether 2022-23 is a genuine one-off event to treat as an outlier in the experience study or a signal that TPD severity/duration pricing and valuation assumptions are understated; coordinate with the IP review since the two lines moved together."
    },
    {
      "benefit": "IP",
      "years": [2022, 2023],
      "pattern": "shock",
      "direction": "increase",
      "magnitude": "flat-topped level jump of ~+0.14 A/E (from ~0.97 baseline to ~1.11) across 2022-2023 (~+14% overpayment), then reversion to 0.93 in 2024",
      "confidence": 0.85,
      "evidence": [
        "ae_ip_by_year.csv: 2022 AE=1.103 (1951/1768) and 2023 AE=1.116 (2094/1876) vs a 2015-2021 baseline of 0.919-1.022",
        "Evidence pack [IP]: excursion 2022-2023 +0.143 vs rest of series, score 9.9; z+4.3 and z+5.0",
        "ae_ip_by_year.csv: abrupt 2021->2022 step (+0.107), essentially flat 2022->2023 (+0.013), sharp 2023->2024 drop (-0.189) — a 2-year level change, not a sustained ramp",
        "summary.json: IP overall_ae 1.002 and overall_termination_ae 0.996, so termination (recovery) rates are NOT the driver; the lift is in claims A/E",
        "Co-occurs in the same 2022-2023 window with the TPD overpayment, indicating a common cause rather than two independent events"
      ],
      "recommended_action": "Prioritise a joint root-cause investigation with TPD because both disability lines overpaid in 2022-2023 and both reverted in 2024. Confirm the lift is driven by claims incidence/severity rather than recovery by checking ae_ip_termination_by_month.csv and ae_ip_termination.csv for 2022-2023 by diagnosis/duration (pooled termination A/E is ~1.0, so termination rates look stable).     }
  ]
}

Here it does NOT rise year over year before peaking: it jumps from 1.03 (2021) to 1.17 (2022) in one step, holds flat at 1.16 (2023), then drops. So it's a flat-topped 2-year excursion = shock. I'll fold this into the recommended_action of both findings and emphasize in overall.

Direction: increase. Magnitude: ~+0.2 A/E (level jump from ~0.94 to ~1.17), i.e., ~+20% overpayment, sustained 2 years, then reverts. Confidence: high (0.9) — both excursion years z>5, score 12.9.
